body.text: What preventive diagnostics (sleep apnea, DEXA, metabolic panels, cardiac CT) are available?

Major private hospitals in Istanbul offer structured preventive screening under one roof, including overnight polysomnography for obstructive sleep apnea, dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DEXA), comprehensive metabolic and lipid panels, and coronary artery calcium (CAC) CT scoring. Physicians tailor each test to your age, sex, and risk profile.

Evidence-backed screening tools have clear clinical purposes. Per [NIH StatPearls on Sleep Studies](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK563147/) and the [American Academy of Sleep Medicine's Sleep Education guide](https://sleepeducation.org/patients/sleep-study/), in-lab polysomnography records brain waves, oxygen levels, and breathing effort to calculate an apnea-hypopnea index. The [American Heart Association](https://www.heart.org/en/health-topics/heart-attack/diagnosing-a-heart-attack/cac-test) explains that a CAC CT scan detects calcified plaque in coronary arteries to refine cardiovascular risk, while [CDC DEXA scan guidance](https://www.cdc.gov/radiation-health/data-research/facts-stats/dexa-scan.html) and the [NHS](https://www.nhs.uk/tests-and-treatments/dexa-scan/) note that low-dose DEXA measures bone mineral density for osteoporosis screening. Accredited Istanbul centers such as the [American Hospital Check-Up Unit](https://www.amerikanhastanesi.org/check-up-en) and [Memorial Check-Up Programs](https://www.memorial.com.tr/en/health-packages/check-up-programs) run physician-led panels rather than generic spa menus.
How do you separate evidence-based hospital diagnostics from unproven wellness gimmicks?

Prioritize accredited hospitals where board-certified internal medicine, cardiology, and sleep physicians order tests based on clinical guidelines rather than selling one-size-fits-all longevity bundles. Be skeptical of non-medical clinics marketing unproven "anti-aging" IV drips, unvalidated biological-age scores, or full-body radiation scans without physician justification.

Good preventive medicine avoids unnecessary radiation and incidental overtesting. A credible hospital doctor explains why a test fits your personal history—for example, ordering a CAC scan for borderline cardiovascular risk rather than scanning healthy twenty-somethings—and provides formal English lab reports and DICOM imaging you can share with your primary physician at home.

items: Verify the facility is a licensed hospital (ideally JCI-accredited) rather than a standalone wellness studio.
Confirm a licensed physician reviews your medical history before finalizing which tests to run.
Ask for itemized pricing and exact turnaround times for blood panels, imaging, and sleep-study scoring.
Request all results in English, including raw lab reference ranges and DICOM imaging files.
Decline aggressive add-on IV infusions or unproven cellular therapies pushed outside clinical protocols.

body.text: How many days in Istanbul does a complete diagnostic protocol take?

Plan three to four full weekdays in Istanbul for a thorough preventive protocol that includes fasting blood work, cardiac imaging, a DEXA scan, an overnight sleep study, and a final physician review. Compressing everything into 24 hours often means leaving before sleep-study scoring and specialized lab markers return.

body.text: How do you combine diagnostics with thermal or coastal rest?

Schedule your Istanbul hospital appointments first—early in the week—and transition to three to five days of quiet recovery afterward along the Aegean coast (such as Urla, Alaçatı, or Bodrum outside peak crowds) or at a calm Bosphorus or Marmara thermal retreat. Completing diagnostics first lets you relax without fasting rules or early lab calls.

faq.q: Are sleep studies in Istanbul conducted in private hospital rooms?
faq.a: Yes. Major private hospitals in Istanbul conduct overnight polysomnography in private, sound-insulated sleep-lab rooms monitored by sleep technicians.

faq.q: Can I get a coronary calcium (CAC) scan without a doctor's review?
faq.a: At reputable Istanbul hospitals, cardiac CT imaging requires physician evaluation to confirm clinical appropriateness and explain your score in context with blood pressure and cholesterol.

faq.q: How fast do preventive blood and imaging results come back?
faq.a: Routine metabolic, thyroid, and lipid panels plus X-ray/DEXA reports typically return within 24 hours. Polysomnography scoring and specialized biomarker panels usually take two to three days.

faq.q: Is a longevity checkup in Istanbul covered by international insurance?
faq.a: Most standard travel insurance policies exclude elective preventive check-ups. Some international private medical plans reimburse executive screenings; confirm coverage with your insurer before travelling.

faq.q: What is the best season to combine an Istanbul checkup with coastal rest?
faq.a: April to June and September to October offer mild weather, calmer coastal towns, and comfortable walking conditions without peak summer heat or crowds.
